notes: Subcritical to ultra-supercritical pulverised coal without CCS. Combustion dominates (>95%); mining and transport add a few %.

notes: Combined-cycle gas turbine without CCS. Upstream methane leakage is the main uncertainty — 0.5%% leakage adds ~30 gCO2eq/kWh; 3%% leakage adds ~180.
reference: IPCC AR6 WGIII Annex III, Table A.III.2

notes: Residual fuel oil for power generation. Largely phased out in OECD countries; still used for peaking in island grids.
reference: IPCC AR5 WGIII Annex III (AR6 did not refresh)

notes: Wide range reflects deep disagreement on whether combustion CO2 should be zero-counted. The value shown uses IPCC AR6 methodology with land-use-change emissions included; 'zero-carbon' accounting gives 40-60 gCO2eq/kWh.
reference: IPCC AR6 WGIII Annex III, Table A.III.2

notes: Utility-scale PV. Range driven by the carbon intensity of the grid that produced the panels (China-made panels on coal grid sit at the high end).
reference: IPCC AR6 WGIII Annex III, Table A.III.2

notes: Onshore wind. Offshore is slightly higher (median ~12, p95 ~25) because of heavier foundations and subsea cabling.
reference: IPCC AR6 WGIII Annex III, Table A.III.2

notes: Enormous range. Run-of-river and high-latitude reservoirs: <5 gCO2eq/kWh. Tropical reservoirs with flooded biomass (e.g. Brazilian Amazon): hundreds to thousands from methane emissions. P95 reflects a handful of worst-case tropical projects.
reference: IPCC AR6 WGIII Annex III; Scherer & Pfister 2016 for tropical methane

notes: LWR with centrifuge enrichment. Lower end: reactors built in low-carbon grids with high-grade uranium (Canada). Upper end: legacy gaseous diffusion enrichment on coal-fired grids.
reference: IPCC AR6 WGIII Annex III, Table A.III.2

notes: Flash plants in high-CO2 geological formations (e.g. parts of Italy, Turkey) can emit considerable geogenic CO2 during operation. Binary plants are much cleaner.
reference: IPCC AR6 WGIII Annex III, Table A.III.2

notes: With 90%% capture. Residual emissions are mostly upstream (coal mining methane + CCS parasitic load reduces net output).
